_comment: Scenario catalogue of the CTTE dashboard (2026-07-28).
Each scenario describes ONE app loadable on the KV260: bitstream (xmutil app name),
aperture regions, CTRL register map, cores/encoders, sinks, console and
decode configuration. The UI builds block diagram and control panel from it,
the server its /dev/mem mappings and register accesses.
WHY this file exists: the CTRL register maps of the apps are NOT
identical. mbv/trio have 0x10 AXIS_BEATS and 0x14 TRACE_BUFSZ; the Linux CVA6
has 0x10 TRACE_BUFSZ, 0x14 CON_BYTES, 0x18 CON_DROPS and shifts everything from
SINK_CTRL up by four bytes. A server with hard-wired offsets silently reads
wrong numbers on whichever app it was not written for.
The register map of every scenario is verified against the RTL:
mbv          rtl/board_kv260/mbv_soc_top.sv (header comment + rdata_q case)
trio         rtl/board_kv260/trio_soc_top.sv
cva6_linux   rtl/board_kv260/cva6_linux_soc_top.sv
cva6_linux64 rtl/board_kv260/cva6_linux64_soc_top.sv (rdata_q case 4'd0..4'd14)
rocket64     vivado/kv260_app/rocket_soc_top.sv (header comment + rdata_q case 5'd0..5'd21)
app_variants (since 2026-08-08): a scenario can be present on the board in
several bitstreams that can be told apart ONLY by the app name. The
address width of the encoder (CT_XLEN) is a synthesis parameter and is held in
no CSR (package W1) -- the name is the only discriminator. An
RV64 core under a 32-bit encoder delivers addresses truncated in HARDWARE;
the dashboard states that instead of computing them back.

scenarios.title: CVA6 · Linux 6.12
scenarios.subtitle: A RISC-V Linux in the PL — and its instruction flow, without the core noticing
headline: Linux 6.12.19 boots on our CVA6 in the KV260 PL, and the boot is fully
recorded as CTTE: 64,651,219 instructions, 0 errors,
6.84 bit per instruction.

cores.name: CVA6
cores.note: OpenSBI + Linux from the reserved PS-DDR window
cores.desc: Linux-capable CVA6 (vendored cva6_ref, OpenHW): RV32IMA_Zicsr_Zifencei, Sv32 MMU, M/S/U, one commit port, no C extension, no FPU, no PMP, 8 KiB I$ / 8 KiB D$. NO local RAM: code and data are fetched over its own 64-bit AXI master from the reserved PS-DDR window @ 0x6400_0000 (+64 MiB, ctrace_resmem.dtso). The PS loads OpenSBI + Linux into that window while core_run=0, configures the encoder, then releases the core.
cores.ingress_desc: cva6_iti (upstream Instruction Trace Interface, E-Trace v2.0.2 ingress, incl. Accemic fixes D1/D2) + cva6_iti_to_ctte_tip shim: the E-Trace itype vocabulary maps value-identically onto the CTTE TIP; trap beats are forced to iretire=0 (CTTE/AMD ICNT convention).

_console_comment: 'interactive' and 'wrapping' describe what the LOADED BITSTREAM can do,
not what the UI would like. Up to bitstream v6, cva6_linux_periph was
TX-only (RBR reads 0, LSR.DR stays 0) and the ring ended after 64 KiB.
The RX bitstream (CON_TX 0x34 / CON_RPTR 0x38) can do both.
The server checks this at run time via CON_TX and corrects the
entry -- if 'true' is stated here and the bitstream cannot do it, input
stays blocked instead of sending characters into the void.

console.note_readonly: This bitstream has no UART RX path: the 8250 is TX-only (RBR reads 0, LSR.DR stays 0). Input requires the RX bitstream.

_decode_comment: live_pcinfo is the SLIM variant for the rolling window.
Measured on the KV260 (Cortex-A53): NexRv reads the pcinfo in full on EVERY
call. The 114 MiB listing of the Linux boot costs 18.06 s per
window -- and 18.08 s with a zero-byte trace as well, so the decode itself
is free. With the 775 KiB OpenSBI listing it is 0.14 s.
Without that separation the live view is unusable on the board.
_symbols_comment: Fallback set for demo mode: ONLY the OpenSBI phase (748 symbols,
24 KiB) -- exactly what the shipped trace excerpt covers.
The FULL set (83,074 symbols from merged3.dis, ~2.7 MiB + 6.2 MiB sites)
is not versioned but produced on the board and then sits next to it as
_code_regions_comment: Address regions for the coverage treemap. A Linux boot runs through
kernel physical until satp is set, kernel virtual afterwards. Without that
separation the same functions would lie twice in one area.

fifo._src: ct_pkg.sv of the built profile: ETIP_CVS_FIFO_DEPTH = (CT_EN_DATA_TRACE||CT_EN_ACT||CT_EN_DAQ) ? 128 : 32

demo._src: Derived from the verified boot record (64,651,219 instructions x 6.84 bpi / 8 = 55.3 MB) and the console boot time up to login (~50 s, kernel timestamps up to 46.7 s): ~1.1 MB/s. bpi 6.84 from the record; without a retires register the UI computes no bpi here.

scenarios.title: CVA6 RV64 · Linux (cv64a6, Sv39)
scenarios.subtitle: A 64-bit RISC-V Linux in the PL — traced with 64-bit addresses
_app_variants_comment: Two bitstreams, one design. The difference is CT_XLEN -- the
address width of the encoder -- and that is a synthesis parameter, not a
CSR (package W1). Whoever loads the 32-bit variant gets addresses
truncated by the HARDWARE; that is not a display error, and it is not

app_variants.label: 64-bit encoder + 16-bit context (CT_CONTEXT_WIDTH=16)
app_variants.note: Adds the Ownership/Context path: satp.ASID reaches the encoder and the comparator can filter on it, so a trace can be restricted to a single Linux process (package W5). Same addresses as the plain 64-bit variant; the context width costs no timing (WNS +1.174 ns vs +1.077, and 421 LUT fewer).

app_variants.label: 64-bit encoder (CT_XLEN=64)
app_variants.note: Full RV64 addresses in the trace stream. No context path: this build predates CT_CONTEXT_WIDTH, emits zero Ownership messages, and satp.ASID is not even wired to the encoder — an ownership filter cannot work here.

app_variants.label: 32-bit encoder (CT_XLEN=32)
app_variants.note: The ENCODER truncates addresses to 32 bit. Sv39 kernel PCs (0xFFFFFFFF8...) cannot be reconstructed from this stream — that is hardware, not display.

headline: Linux 6.x boots on our 64-bit CVA6 (cv64a6_imac_sv39, no FPU) in the
KV260 PL: 'buildroot login:', isa rv64imac_zicsr_zifencei_zca, mmu sv39.
RV64 PC decode is proven at the board: 818,663 instructions from one
stream, 0 errors — the majority of them above 2^32 (package W1).
_ctrl_comment: Word for word the map of the RV32 version -- that is intentional and is
recorded as such in the file header of cva6_linux64_soc_top.sv, so that the
PS tools keep working unchanged. Verified against the rdata_q case
(4'd0..4'd14) of the same file, not copied from the RV32 row.

cores.name: CVA6
cores.mhz_note: Design constrained to 75 MHz. The board's boot firmware leaves pl_clk0 at 100 MHz; the board runners set 75 MHz explicitly (vivado/kv260_app/kv260_plclk.sh).
cores.note: OpenSBI + RV64 Linux from the reserved PS-DDR window
cores.desc: 64-bit CVA6 (vendored cva6_ref, OpenHW), configuration delta D6: RV64IMAC_Zicsr_Zifencei_Zca, Sv39 MMU, M/S/U, one commit port, NO FPU, 8 KiB I$ / 8 KiB D$. Code and data come over its own 64-bit AXI master from the reserved PS-DDR window @ 0x6400_0000 (192 MiB). Three RV64 deltas in the SoC hull were each a boot stopper on their own: RISCV_WORD_WIDTH=64 at the atomics block (otherwise every amoadd.d and thus every kernel spinlock fails), byte-strobe-exact 64-bit CLINT writes (otherwise mtimecmp[63:32] keeps its reset value and the timer never fires), and msip routed to the core.
cores.ingress_desc: cva6_iti (E-Trace v2.0.2 ingress, incl. Accemic fixes D1/D2) + cva6_iti_to_ctte_tip shim, width-parametric: the same shim carries 32- and 64-bit addresses.

console.note_readonly: This bitstream has no UART RX path: the 8250 is TX-only. Input requires an RX-capable bitstream.

_decode_comment: There is NO pcinfo for this core in the tree -- the RV64 listing of the
Linux image is produced on the board (sw/cva6_linux/make_listing_rv64.sh) and
is too large to be versioned. The server looks for it as
pcinfo_cva6_linux64_src0.pcinfo        (full)
pcinfo_cva6_linux64_src0_live.pcinfo   (slim, for the live window)
in the dashboard directory. If it is missing, the live view says exactly that --
it shows no invented names.
_code_regions_comment: Three spaces as in the RV32 boot, but on RV64 the third one is NOT at
PAGE_OFFSET but in the topmost 2 GiB: 0xFFFFFFFF_8000_0000
is the reason for the 64-bit address display -- read as a 32-bit number

scenarios.title: Rocket RV64 · Linux (Rocket64t1)
scenarios.subtitle: A second, foreign 64-bit core — same encoder, same stream format

app_variants.label: 64-bit encoder (CT_XLEN=64)
app_variants.note: Full RV64 addresses in the trace stream. Built with EN_ETRACE=0.

app_variants.label: 32-bit encoder (CT_XLEN=32)
app_variants.note: The ENCODER truncates addresses to 32 bit. PC_LO/PC_HI still carry the full 64-bit retired PC — that path is width-agnostic and independent of the encoder.

headline: The same CTTE encoder on a core we did not build: SiFive's Rocket
(Rocket64t1, RV64IMAC, no FPU) boots Linux in the KV260 PL —
'buildroot login:', uarch sifive,rocket0, marchid 0x1.
_ctrl_comment: ONE row more than in the CVA6 design: window-guard diagnostics (0x3C..0x44),
PLIC inputs (0x48) and the 64-bit PC (0x4C/0x50) plus retire counter
(0x54). Source is the header comment of vivado/kv260_app/rocket_soc_top.sv,
cross-read against the rdata_q case (5'd0..5'd21) of the same file.
_core_pc_comment: The observation channel of this design (lesson C6 from the trio): without it
'core hangs' cannot be told apart from 'window guard has tripped'.
PC_LO/PC_HI are built width-agnostic -- on the
32-bit encoder build PC_HI reads 0, with CT_XLEN=64 the same logic carries
the full RV64 PC without changing a line of RTL.

cores.name: Rocket
cores.mhz_note: Design constrained to 75 MHz; the board runners set pl_clk0 explicitly (vivado/kv260_app/kv260_plclk.sh).
cores.panel: Rocket64t1 — a core we did not build
cores.desc: Generated core (rocket-chip, Rocket64t1): RV64IMAC, no FPU, CLINT + PLIC + bootrom are INSIDE the generated netlist. It sees its RAM at guest address 0x8000_0000; a window guard in the wrapper translates that to the reserved PS-DDR window at 0x6400_0000 and reports every rejected access (WIN_ERR_*). The A extension is resolved inside the core (TLAtomicAutomata / L1D), so no atomics block is needed on the AXI side.
cores.ingress_desc: Rocket's trace port (TCI) is converted to the RISC-V TIP by a width-parametric shim — the same TIP the encoder consumes in every other scenario of this dashboard. One encoder, one stream format, a different ingress vocabulary per core family.

console.note_readonly: No UART RX path in this bitstream: RBR reads 0, LSR.DR stays 0.

_decode_comment: As with cv64a6: the listing is produced on the board, the server looks for
pcinfo_rocket64_src0.pcinfo (+ _live). If it is missing, the view says so.

scenarios.subtitle: Two harts, two encoders, one merged stream — and it separates again

installed on THIS board is decided by `xmutil listapps` -- and the server
answers that at run time. If the app is not in the list, the header
greys the button out instead of offering a load that ends with
headline: Two Rocket harts, one CTTE encoder each, ONE merged ATB stream:
SMP Linux boots on both (Platform HART Count : 2, 'smp: Brought up
1 node, 2 CPUs'), and the merged stream splits again by Nexus SRC —
1,475,706 / 1,665,826 PCs bare metal, gapless, in disjoint regions
(packages M4/M5). Under Linux the two streams are told apart by the
Ownership context: five satp contexts per SRC, sets disjoint (M6).
_ctrl_comment: 0x00..0x54 identical to rocket64 -- intentional, so that the existing
board scripts keep working. NEW are only 0x58 FUNNEL_CTRL and the
second observation set 0x5C/0x60/0x64 for hart 1. Source is the
header comment of vivado/kv260_app/rocket2_soc_top.sv, cross-read
against the rdata_q case of the same file.
_core_pc_comment: Observation channel PER HART (M4 item 3): with two harts 'the core hangs'
is not one question but two -- a shared
retire counter would keep running happily while ONE hart stands still. The
instrument here shows hart 0; STATUS b18/b19 carry retire_seen per
hart, b[22:20] the privilege level of hart 1, and b8 is deliberately the
OR of both harts, so that the single-hart scripts stay readable.

cores.name: Rocket hart 0
cores.mhz_note: Design constrained to 75 MHz; the board runners set pl_clk0 explicitly (vivado/kv260_app/kv260_plclk.sh). Post-route WNS +3.466 ns, 47,019 LUT (40.2 %) / 9,320 CLB (63.7 %) — smaller AND faster than the single-hart build (M4).
cores.desc: First hart of a two-hart Rocket (rocket-chip generator, RV64IMAC, no FPU, TLBroadcast instead of L2). CLINT + PLIC + bootrom are inside the generated netlist; both harts share ONE mem_axi4 and ONE mmio_axi4, so the board wrapper needs no second memory path (M4). Its own CTTE instance sits at ENC0 @ 0xA001_0000 and is set to SrcID 0 — that field is what the decoder uses to take the merged stream apart again.
cores.ingress_desc: Rocket's trace port (TCI) converted to the RISC-V TIP by a width-parametric shim, one per hart. The shim also carries the per-hart context (satp) to the encoder: trace_core_0_context[63:0], of which CT_CONTEXT_WIDTH=22 bits are wired (M3).
facts: satp.PPN -> ctx[43:0], 22 bit wired, NO reset value (M3-2)

cores.name: Rocket hart 1
cores.desc: Second hart of the same generated core. It has no memory of its own — one image, one window, brought up by SMP Linux ('Platform HART Count : 2'). What it DOES have of its own is a full CTTE instance at ENC1 @ 0xA002_0000 with SrcID 1, its own observation channel (0x5C/0x60/0x64) and its own context path. Start/stop is shared: CONTROL b0 holds both harts.
cores.ingress_desc: Second, identical shim on trace_core_1_*. The port comparison RocketSystem t1 -> t2 shows the delta is exactly this: resetctrl_hartIsInReset_1 plus the complete trace_core_1_* set (M4).

_console_comment: Register map checked against vivado/kv260_app/rocket2_soc_top.sv, not
copied from rocket64: rdata_q case 5'd5 = CON_BYTES (0x14),
5'd6 = CON_DROPS (0x18), 5'd13 = CON_TX (0x34), 5'd14 = CON_RPTR
offset delivers SILENTLY wrong characters here, hence the comparison.
NO note_readonly: this build has the RX path (con_rx_wr /
con_rx_data / con_rx_used / con_rx_drops, write access 0x34 b8),
and M5 §4.1 logged in over it and issued commands
('CPU0  CPU1' from /proc/interrupts IN THE GUEST). The note came from
rocket64 and would be an unsubstantiated restriction here.
_decode_comment: Two targets in ONE stream. The funnel merges message-atomically; the
separation happens host-side on the Nexus SRC field (SrcBits 2). The
counter-check from M5 belongs to the statement: with BOTH encoders on SrcID 0
the separation fails (source 1: 0 PCs).

demo._src: Live board session 2026-08-11 (Rocket64t2, SMP Linux): dashboard header 633,277 and 633,734 B/s, bpi panel 3.0 - screenshots c-trace_marketing/paper/fig/dashboard.png + dashboard-dark.png. Values for the DemoBus simulation, so that fill bars and bpi show the order of magnitude seen on the board.

scenarios.title: CVA6 RV64 · 2 cores · AMP (cv64a6)
scenarios.subtitle: Two independent RV64 cores, two encoders, one merged stream
_amp_comment: AMP, not SMP -- and that is a decision, not a shortcoming. In this tree the
core carries NOC_TYPE_AXI4_ATOP and no L1 coherency path (the
OpenPiton attachment sits behind an ifdef and is not compiled).
Two cores on ONE cached window would be incoherent, and the
failure mode would be silent data corruption. Therefore: one private
cached 32 MiB window per core with its own PS port; the only thing shared is
an UNCACHED mailbox from 0x6800_0000 -- coherent by construction, because
no cache is involved at all. The synchronization over it is carried by ONE
common atomics instance behind the merge; two separate ones would be
ineffective between the cores (axi_res_tbl clears address-equal and ID-blind,
package L1, 15/15 with a red mutation probe).
_sendcfg_comment: OPERATING DIFFERENCE, belongs in BOTH scenarios (requirement D-R-9 item 4): the
SENDCFG=once obligation depends on the ENCODER knob CT_XLEN, not on the
core width. With CT_XLEN=64 it is MANDATORY -- only from the config message
does the decoder read CAPS bit 23 and switch to 64 bit. With CT_XLEN=32
it is unnecessary. As of 2026-08-10 BOTH builds carry the profile ctte_slim64
(CT_XLEN=64), so that the area figures stay comparable (D-R-9 item 2)
-- so SENDCFG=once applies in the RV32 build too. As soon as a CT_XLEN=32
profile exists, enc_xlen AND this note change; there is no such encoder
build in the repo today (all bld/*/ctte_* carry CT_XLEN=64).
_loadable_comment: The bitstream has NOT been loaded on the board -- the two-hart Rocket
demonstration is running there (as of 2026-08-10). Whether the app is installed
on this board is answered by 'xmutil listapps' at run time; if it is not in
the list, the header greys the button out instead of offering a
load that ends with 'app not found'.
headline: Two cv64a6 cores, one CTTE encoder each, ONE merged ATB stream that
splits again by Nexus SRC, exactly as in rocket2.
AMP, not SMP: this core has no L1 coherence path, so each core owns a
private cached 32 MiB window on its own PS HP port, and the two share
only an UNCACHED mailbox at 0x6800_0000 — coherent by construction,
because no cache is involved. LR/SC over it works because ONE shared
atomics instance sits behind the merge; its reservation table is ID-blind.
_ctrl_comment: 0x00..0x44 and 0x4C..0x64 are IDENTICAL to rocket2 -- intentional, so that the
existing board scripts and the dashboard map keep working unchanged.
NEW are 0x68/0x6C/0x70 (second window guard -- this build has TWO
separate memory windows, rocket2 has one) and 0x74 (guard of the
shared mailbox). 0x48 stays FREE: on rocket2 it holds EXT_IRQ for
the PLIC of the generated core, and this build has no PLIC. Source is the
header comment of rtl/board_kv260/cva6_2_soc_top.sv, cross-read against the
rdata_q case of the same file (5'd15..5'd29).
_core_pc_comment: Observation channel PER CORE: with two cores 'the core hangs' is not
one question but two -- a shared retire counter would keep running
happily while ONE core stands still. The instrument here shows core 0; STATUS
b18/b19 carry retire_seen per core, b[22:20] the privilege level of core 1,
and b8 is deliberately the OR of both cores, so that the single-core scripts
stay readable. b[14:12] and b[22:20] are three bits wide although CVA6
delivers only two -- the upper position is fixed 0, so that the map stays
bit-identical to rocket2.

cores.name: cv64a6 core 0
cores.mhz_note: Design constrained to 75 MHz. D2 measured the lower bound (2 cores + 2 encoders + funnel, no memory path): 88.99 % CLB, routed at WNS +0.249 ns / WHS +0.035 ns. The full build adds memory path, periph and sinks — measured in package D3.
cores.mem: guest 0x6400_0000 +32 MiB cached -> PS DDR 0x6400_0000 (private); mailbox guest 0x6800_0000 +16 MiB uncached -> PS DDR 0x6800_0000 (shared)
cores.desc: First cv64a6 (OpenHW's core, RV64IMAC, no FPU, Sv39, S+U, NrCommitPorts=1). It owns a private 32 MiB guest window at 0x6400_0000 translated to PS DDR 0x6400_0000, reached over its OWN PS port (S_AXI_HP1) through its OWN atomics instance — core 1 never touches this memory. Its CTTE instance sits at ENC0 @ 0xA001_0000 and is set to SrcID 0; that field is what the decoder uses to take the merged stream apart again.
cores.ingress_desc: The core's instruction-trace interface (ITI) converted to the RISC-V TIP by a width-parametric shim, one per core. The context path is OFF in this build: the shim wires satp.ASID only when TIP_CONTEXT_WIDTH equals Cfg.ASIDW, and the slim64 encoder profile carries 22 (satp.PPN of the Rocket generator) while this core has 16. A silently truncated identifier would name the wrong process, so it is left out rather than shortened.
facts: own 32 MiB window, own PS HP port (HP1), own atomics
WIN_ERR_* @ 0x3C, burst envelope checked, DECERR on miss
shared with the other core (CONTROL b0)

cores.name: cv64a6 core 1
cores.mem: guest 0x6400_0000 +32 MiB cached -> PS DDR 0x6600_0000 (private); mailbox guest 0x6800_0000 +16 MiB uncached -> PS DDR 0x6800_0000 (shared)
cores.desc: Second cv64a6, identical configuration — the cores differ ONLY in where their window lands in PS DDR (0x6600_0000 instead of 0x6400_0000) and in the hart ID. It runs its own image: AMP means two guests, not one kernel on two harts. Own encoder at ENC1 @ 0xA002_0000 with SrcID 1, own observation channel (0x5C/0x60/0x64), own window guard (0x68/0x6C/0x70). Start/stop is shared: CONTROL b0 holds both cores.
cores.ingress_desc: The core's instruction-trace interface (ITI) converted to the RISC-V TIP by a width-parametric shim, one per core. The context path is OFF in this build: the shim wires satp.ASID only when TIP_CONTEXT_WIDTH equals Cfg.ASIDW, and the slim64 encoder profile carries 22 (satp.PPN of the Rocket generator) while this core has 16. A silently truncated identifier would name the wrong process, so it is left out rather than shortened.
facts: own 32 MiB window, own PS HP port (HP2), own atomics
WIN1_ERR_* @ 0x68, burst envelope checked, DECERR on miss
shared with the other core (CONTROL b0)

_console_comment: ONE console for BOTH cores, deliberately: under AMP two independent
guests write into the same ring, the output interleaves. That is the same
picture as on the two-hart Rocket and is not to be mistaken for a defect.
Two rings would have needed a second CON aperture and would have broken the
requirement 'congruent view' (D-R-9). Whoever wants to separate the sources
separates them at the trace (Nexus SRC), not at the console. The RX path is
present (con_rx_wr/con_rx_data/con_rx_used, write access CON_TX b8).
_decode_comment: Two targets in ONE stream. The funnel merges message-atomically; the
separation happens host-side on the Nexus SRC field (SrcBits 2). Unlike on
rocket2, the two cores HERE carry SEPARATE images -- one pcinfo per core,
because they do not see the same memory (AMP).

headline: Two cv32a6 cores, one CTTE encoder each, ONE merged ATB stream — the
same picture as the RV64 variant, and deliberately so: same block order,
same labels, same register map, same geometry. Only the core differs.
AMP applies unchanged: NOC_TYPE_AXI4_ATOP is a property of how the core
attaches, not of the register width, so the space saved does not buy
coherence. What it does buy is room — D2 measured 34.87 % CLB against
88.99 % for RV64 in the same lower-bound cut, at five times the margin.

separate memory windows, rocket2 has one) and 0x74 (guard of the
shared mailbox). 0x48 stays FREE: on rocket2 it holds EXT_IRQ for
the PLIC of the generated core, and this build has no PLIC. Source is the
header comment of rtl/board_kv260/cva6_2_soc_top.sv, cross-read against the
rdata_q case of the same file (5'd15..5'd29).
_core_pc_comment: Observation channel PER CORE: with two cores 'the core hangs' is not
one question but two -- a shared retire counter would keep running
happily while ONE core stands still. The instrument here shows core 0; STATUS
b18/b19 carry retire_seen per core, b[22:20] the privilege level of core 1,
and b8 is deliberately the OR of both cores, so that the single-core scripts
stay readable. b[14:12] and b[22:20] are three bits wide although CVA6
delivers only two -- the upper position is fixed 0, so that the map stays
bit-identical to rocket2.

_console_comment: ONE console for BOTH cores, deliberately: under AMP two independent
guests write into the same ring, the output interleaves. That is the same
picture as on the two-hart Rocket and is not to be mistaken for a defect.
Two rings would have needed a second CON aperture and would have broken the
requirement 'congruent view' (D-R-9). Whoever wants to separate the sources
separates them at the trace (Nexus SRC), not at the console. The RX path is
present (con_rx_wr/con_rx_data/con_rx_used, write access CON_TX b8).
_decode_comment: Two targets in ONE stream. The funnel merges message-atomically; the
separation happens host-side on the Nexus SRC field (SrcBits 2). Unlike on
rocket2, the two cores HERE carry SEPARATE images -- one pcinfo per core,
because they do not see the same memory (AMP).

app_variants.label: D1 build (15 WP slots, direct window)
app_variants.note: Pre-D2 bitstream: 256 KiB URAM ring and no sink window -- 0x18..0x38 read 0 and writes are no-ops, so DDR and PIB are simply not there (not switched off).

app_variants.label: C0b build (1023 WP slots indirect + AXIS timestamp)
app_variants.note: The G1 live-demo bitstream: 256 KiB URAM ring, no sink window (0x18..0x38 read 0). DDR and PIB arrive with the C0B_SINK3 build.

app_variants.label: C0B_SINK3 build (three sinks: URAM 1 MiB + DDR4 256 MiB + PIB; U1 per-core run bits, U9-1 read-only window)
app_variants.note: Same encoder and watchpoint set as C0b, plus the shared three-sink subsystem (ct_trace_sinks, package T2): the URAM ring grows to 1 MiB, the DDR4 sink writes into the reserved PS-DDR window, and the parallel port drives PMOD J2. Sinks are reset-inert (SINK_CTRL=0), so the wire stream is byte-identical to C0b until one is switched on. Rebuilt for package U6 (2026-08-15): the DDR window resets to 0x5000_0000 + 256 MiB (address plan v4) and DDR_BASE/DDR_SIZE are refused while the sink is armed, with SINK_STAT b4 ddr_cfg_rej as the reason. SAME app name for all three builds, so xmutil cannot tell them apart; the bitstream is identified by md5 6dd0778b842e16f145af81c1df2e3ca8 (U1 was 0378884e…, T2 f9ff404d…). On a pre-U6 bitstream the window still resets to 0x6000_0000 + 64 MiB and b4 stays 0 — the cards read the registers, so they follow whichever build is loaded; on a pre-U1 bitstream the per-core buttons write bits that nothing reads and STATUS b8/b9 stay 0, which is exactly what the server reports back as a hint. Rebuilt again for package U11 (2026-08-16): the vendored encoder now carries the U10 CSR audit (the eight trTeInstFeatures.InstEn* bits and the DF range memory mem1 are Enable-locked, so a write while the encoder is armed is refused with 409 instead of vanishing), and DDR_BASE/DDR_SIZE are READ-ONLY IN HARDWARE (U9-1): a write is discarded whether the sink is armed or not, the registers always read the reset window, and SINK_STAT b4 latches every refused attempt. Predecessors: U6 fef8ace2, U1 0378884e, T2 f9ff404d.

_comment: AXIS watchpoint testbed (packages D0/D1/E0/F0/F1/G0/H).
app_variants (2026-08-14, package T2/T3): tgc5b2_axis_wp_c0b_sink3
brings the shared three-sink subsystem (ct_trace_sinks) -- CTRL
0x18..0x38 offset-identical to duo, URAM ring 1 MiB instead of 256 KiB,
DDR_BEATS at 0x38 (in the C0B_DDR build the counter was at 0x30, where
PIB_DROPS sits now; docs/SPEC_axis_wp_memory_map.md §9). The two older
variants therefore carry a 'sinks' entry of their own: in them the
sink registers read 0 -- the view claims no sink there that
the loaded bitstream does not have.
app_variants (2026-08-13, live demo): the C0b rebuild
tgc5b2_axis_wp_c0b (1023 WP indirect + AXIS-TS, G1 board E2E green)
is present on the board as an xmutil app of its own -- same window layout /
register map for everything this view reads (WPCTRL/FIFOs
read-only); ONLY /api/wp/load stays bound to D1 (the direct window
0x4100 does not exist in the C0b build -- 409/ineffective there,
loading runs indirectly via tools/axis_wp_host/wp_load_indirect).
Register map from docs/SPEC_axis_wp_memory_map.md, verified on the board
in G0 (docs/handoffs/G0_board_e2e.md: MAGIC, FTIME ~75.8 MHz, 36/36
oracle sequence per core). Two TGC5B cores, each with one CTTE encoder
with watchpoint unit; WP hits leave the encoder as AXIS records
(4 words: PC, slot, TS, meta) through ct_axis_wp_shim into one
axi_fifo_mm_s (PG080) each. FIFO reading is DESTRUCTIVE (every RDFD read
pops) -- only the server drain (wp_view.py) reads the
FIFO windows; avoid /api/read on fifo0/fifo1.
WP expansion (H3, 2026-08-13): C0b bitstream = 1023 WP per encoder
(loaded indirectly) + AXIS-TS (W2 = timestamp, tstrb 0xFFF, G1
board E2E green); the D1 app carries 15 slots over the direct
window +0x4100 and delivers W2 == 0 (tstrb 0x0FF). The view
still checks no TS monotonicity (F1 --ts-mode off applies to
the D1 variant; wp_load_slots caps ONLY the /api/wp/load
direct path, which exists in the D1 app alone).
headline: Both TGC5B cores walk the same watchpoint set (1023 slots on the
C0b bitstream, loaded indirectly; 15 on the D1 app); every hit
leaves the encoder as a 4-word AXIS record with PC, slot, core ID
and — on C0b — an AXIS timestamp.
The live record view is at /wp.html (server-side FIFO drain).

Own 64 KiB RAM @ 0xA010_0000 (accessible only while THIS core is halted), own CTTE encoder at ENC0 with the watchpoint unit armed; WP hits leave as AXIS records into FIFO0 @ 0xA041_0000. Records carry core_id=1 in W3. Since U1 it starts and stops on its own bit (CONTROL b9), independently of core 0; b0 remains the collective bit, effective = b0 | b9 (SPEC §10).

_sinks_comment: Applies to the C0B_SINK3 bitstream (package T2). The two older
app variants carry a 'sinks' entry of their own (see app_variants):
if one of them is loaded, the view shows only the URAM ring.
_sink_defaults_comment: U5 (field report 2026-08-15: 'nothing visibly arrives in DDR4'). SINK_CTRL
is reset-inert, and no path of the dashboard had ever set ddr_en --
the T3 proof did it by hand. The bind now establishes this default
(server.arm_default_sinks, idempotent: if the bits already match,
nothing is written; the pulse bits b1/b5 are ALWAYS masked out).
ddr_circ=1 is deliberately the RING and not one shot: measured in
T3 were ~41.5 MB/s into the 64 MiB window of that time -- one shot stood
at FULL after ~1.6 s, colored the card as an error and afterwards counted
only drops (T3 §7: 15 million in 3 s). The ring keeps the window filled,
the write pointer visibly moves on, and 'full' means there what
it is supposed to mean: the last 256 MiB are ready. Whoever needs the dump
of a completed run switches the DDR card to one shot.
U6/U8 (2026-08-15): the window is now 0x5000_0000 + 256 MiB
(address plan v4, ct_trace_sinks) -- at the 16.7 MB/s measured in U5
the ring wraps after ~16 s instead of after ~4 s. The default itself
does NOT change as a result: it names bits, not addresses, and the
window check reads base and size from the registers.
The target window is checked against /proc/device-tree/
reserved-memory before arming (DDR_BASE 0x5000_0000 +256 MiB lies in
ctrace-pl-ddr@50000000 +512 MiB); without that evidence it is NOT armed.
_decode_comment: H3 (review finding 4, 2026-08-13): pcinfo for the E0 program is now
versioned (sw/axis_wp_demo/axis_wp_demo.pcinfo, NexRv -conv from
axis_wp_demo.dis, build.sh step) -- decode/live_pc are active as a
result. Both cores run THE SAME program in their own RAMs, hence
the same pcinfo per target (pattern rocket2). On the board,
pcinfo_path() first finds pcinfo_tgc5b2_axis_wp_src<t>.pcinfo in the
dashboard folder (deploy), on the workstation the repo path.
The CTRL map of this SoC top has NO HW retire counter
(rdata case 0..4, tgc5b2_axis_soc_top.sv) -- so the fine-window sampler
of the server delivers nothing here (bpi_win.n = 0), and that is
hardware, not an omission in this map.
U5 (field report 2026-08-15, 'bpi chart stays empty'): the chart stood
empty for that reason. It now draws the DECODED size from the
rolling window (/api/livepc -> decode.bits_per_instr: bytes of the
window times 8 divided by the instructions of ALL sources). That is
the same definition, only from the other source -- and the curve says
in its title which one. On scenarios WITH a retire counter everything
stays as before: there the hardware counters win.
_symbols_comment: Canonical next to the program artifacts (pattern wp_set.txt);
The board deploy places copies as
load_symbol_files() finds those as the first candidate.

_wp_comment: All WPCTRL offsets from docs/SPEC_axis_wp_memory_map.md §3 -- here and
not in wp_view.py, for the same reason as the CTRL maps (no
offset as a literal in the server). ftime: reading LO latches the 64-bit
snapshot, HI delivers the upper 32 bits of the one latched last --
ALWAYS LO first. ovf is sticky, clear only via PL reset (D0 #4).
wp_set: PC->symbol name; candidates are searched in wp_view.py in
order (dashboard folder first -- the board deploy puts the file
there -- then the repo path sw/axis_wp_demo/).
wp_slots = 1023 is the C0b state (trWpCap == 1023, loaded indirectly,
G1 board E2E); wp_load_slots = 15 caps EXCLUSIVELY the
POST /api/wp/load path, because that one writes the D1 DIRECT WINDOW
+0x4100 -- which exists only in the D1 app, and there it is 15
slots. The C0b load runs indirectly (tools/axis_wp_host/
wp_load_indirect), not over this endpoint (H3, 2026-08-13).
U4 (2026-08-15): 'wp_table_off' is REMOVED here. The key
stood at 0x4100, and since the C0b rework there is NO register
there any more (SPEC §7, ct_cs_cpuif_wb.sv:220-227) -- the writes went
nowhere and the endpoint still reported ok. Without the key,
load_table rejects the call with the migration recipe instead of
writing ineffectively; the indirect loader in the dashboard remains
the open point H2 (docs/REPORT_axis_wp_completion.md §7). Whoever loads
the D1 app enters the key again -- then the direct path lives on
unchanged.

demo._src: Demo rate freely chosen (smooth table in the browser); the production rate measured on the board is ~21k rec/s per core at a drain of ~12.7k (G0 run B) -- demo mode shows the MECHANISM, not the board load, and states that in the UI.
